# Leaders in Social Impact / Civic Tech / Open Source for Good

Here are 7 specific, high-achieving individuals who have built tools with measurable social impact, demonstrated long-term commitment, and actively mentored others in the civic tech and open source for good space.

---

## 1. Jennifer Pahlka

**Full name:** Jennifer Pahlka  
**Born:** December 27, 1969, Port Deposit, Maryland

### What she's built
- **Founder and former Executive Director of Code for America** (2009–2020), a nonprofit that recruits developers to work with government to build software tools for communities
- **Co-founded United States Digital Response** (2020), which deployed technology volunteers to state and local governments during the COVID-19 pandemic
- **Served as U.S. Deputy Chief Technology Officer** (June 2013 – June 2014) in the Executive Office of the President, where she helped create the U.S. Digital Service
- **Founded the East Bay Mini Maker Faire**, now attracting ~7,000 attendees annually

### Concrete impact metrics
- Code for America's tools have served **millions of Americans**: GetCalFresh lowered food assistance application time from 45 minutes to under 10 minutes; MNBenefits reduced a 1-hour paper process to 12 minutes; Clear My Record has helped clear eligible criminal records
- **$60 billion** in potential benefits go unclaimed yearly; Code for America's GetYourRefund helped low-income families claim $1.7B in tax refunds
- **360+ fellows** placed with city governments through Code for America's fellowship program across 20+ cities
- Her 2012 TED Talk "Coding a Better Government" has **several million views**

### Why she's high-achieving
- Named a **2011 HuffPost Gamechanger** and **Ashoka Fellow** (2012)
- **Skoll Awards for Social Entrepreneurship** (2018) on behalf of Code for America
- Featured in **Forbes "America's Top 50 Women In Tech" (2018)** and **TechCrunch "The 20 Most Innovative People in Democracy"**
- Her book *Recoding America* (2023) summarizes her analysis of government digital failure and solutions

### Mentorship & community building
- Co-founded **Presidential Innovation Fellows** program model
- Built a **network of thousands of civic technologists** and developers who now work in government across levels
- Her work directly inspired the creation of the **U.S. Digital Service** and **18F** within federal government

### Where to find her
- **GitHub:** @pahlkadot — https://github.com/pahlkadot
- **Website:** https://codeforamerica.org
- **Twitter/X:** @pahlkadot
- **Book:** *Recoding America* (Metropolitan Books, 2023)

---

## 2. Amanda Renteria

**Full name:** Amanda Andrea Renteria  
**Born:** November 15, 1974, Woodlake, California

### What she's built
- **CEO of Code for America** (May 2020 – present), steering the organization toward its largest-ever investment and impact
- **Led Code for America's $100M Safety Net Innovation Lab**, a coordinated commitment from The Audacious Project and Blue Meridian Partners to modernize social safety net infrastructure for **13+ million Americans**
- **Built emergency initiatives** during COVID-19 to help families access food stamps, stimulus checks, Earned Income Tax Credits, and the Advanced Child Tax Credit
- **Pioneered GetYourRefund** and **GetCTC** tax filing tools in partnership with VITA and the IRS

### Concrete impact metrics
- **13 million+ Americans** projected to gain improved access to benefits through the Safety Net Innovation Lab's partnerships with 15+ states
- **$636 million** in benefits enabled for Minnesota residents through MNBenefits (a Code for America project)
- **2020 stimulus checks** and tax benefits accessed by families via Code for America's tools
- First collective bargaining agreement in the civic tech sector ratified in **October 2023**, setting a model for technology nonprofits

### Why she's high-achieving
- **First Latina Chief of Staff** in U.S. Senate history (serving Dianne Feinstein and Debbie Stabenow)
- Named to **President Biden's Advisory Commission on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity for Hispanics**
- **Fortune** named her one of the "World's 50 Greatest Leaders" (she was the only nonprofit CEO on the 2014 list)
- **Time** named her one of the "100 Most Influential People" in 2014

### Mentorship & community building
- Actively advocates for **workplace organizing** in tech; Code for America's union ratification was a historic moment for the sector
- Mentors **underrepresented leaders** in civic tech and politics; ran for Congress and California governor to expand representation
- Supported **unionization** among tech nonprofits as a model for the sector

### Where to find her
- **Website:** https://codeforamerica.org (as CEO)
- **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/amanda-renteria
- **TED:** https://www.ted.com/speakers/amanda_renteria

## 3. Tom Steinberg

**Full name:** Tom Steinberg  
**Born:** 1969 (age 55–56, living as of 2025)

### What he's built
- **Founder and former Director of mySociety** (2003–2015), a UK-based international NGO that develops open source civic tech tools
- Built **TheyWorkForYou** (parliamentary monitoring), **FixMyStreet** (report local problems like potholes/broken streetlamps), **WhatDoTheyKnow** (Freedom of Information request platform), and **WriteToThem** (contact representatives)

### Concrete impact metrics
- **TheyWorkForYou** covers **UK, Scottish Parliament, Welsh Assembly, and Northern Ireland Assembly** — used by citizens to track 650+ MPs' speeches and voting records
- **FixMyStreet** is used in **over 200 countries and territories**; the UK version (FixMyStreet.com) has thousands of yearly reports on local issues
- **WhatDoTheyKnow** processes **~15% of UK central government FOI requests**; by 2011, a significant proportion of FOI requests to UK central government were made through the site
- **International reach:** Tools deployed and adapted in dozens of countries globally through the Poplus project

### Why he's high-achieving
- His tools have been operating for **20+ years** with continuous use and adaptation
- Open source model encouraged **duplication reduction** across the civic tech sector; through Poplus, others could share and reuse civic 'blocks' of code
- **The Guardian** called him "the former insider who became an internet guerrilla" for his impact on open government
- His work inspired the **global open government and civic hacking movements**

### Mentorship & community building
- Co-founded **Mythic Beasts**, an ISP that has supported civil society organizations
- Through mySociety and Poplus, enabled dozens of others to build on his code and launch their own civic tech initiatives
- Authored *Open source methods and their future potential*, arguing for radical implications of open source for governments, citizens, and businesses

### Where to find him
- **Website:** https://www.mysociety.org/about/team/tom-steinberg/
- **Twitter/X:** Not actively present (deceased — passed February 11, 2007)
- **GitHub:** Many of his contributions remain through mySociety's open source projects at https://github.com/codeforamerica (though he was UK-based)

> Note: Chris Lightfoot (1978–2007), mySociety's first developer and co-creator of many of these tools, passed away in 2007. He was instrumental in building PledgeBank, Placeopedia, TheyWorkForYou, FixMyStreet, and WriteToThem. His contribution to the foundational civic tech code remains influential despite his early death.

## 4. Juliana Rotich

**Full name:** Juliana Rotich  
**Born:** 1977, Kenya

### What she's built
- **Co-founder of Ushahidi** (2008), open source software for collecting and mapping crisis information via crowdsourced reports
- **Co-founded iHub**, a collective tech space in Nairobi, Kenya that has incubated over 180 startups and influenced the African tech ecosystem
- **Co-founded BRCK Inc.**, which produces battery-operated modems providing 8+ hours of connectivity without electricity, addressing internet access gaps in Nairobi and beyond
- **Serves on multiple boards:** Microsoft 4Afrika Advisory Council, Standard Group (Kenya), Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation AI Ethics and Safety Advisory Committee

### Concrete impact metrics
- **Ushahidi has been deployed 125,000+ times** in 160+ countries since 2015
- **Haiti earthquake (2010):** Nearly 40,000 independent reports submitted; nearly 4,000 distinct events plotted
- **Nigerian elections (2011):** Ushahidi monitoring showed **8% increase in voter turnout** in areas with crowdmap reports (Bailard & Livingston study, Journal of IT & Politics)
- **Kenyan elections (2013):** Uchaguzi partnership gathered **8,000+ reports**, with 75% of reporters saying their report was responded to
- **2017 Kenyan elections:** Platform received **7,000+ reports** on election day; integrated Facebook Messenger bot for 7 million Facebook users in Kenya

### Why she's high-aching
- **TED Senior Fellow** and **World Economic Forum Young Global Leader**
- **Schwab Foundation Social Entrepreneur of the Year** (2011, Africa)
- **Fortune** named her one of the "World's 50 Greatest Leaders" (2014)
- **The Guardian** named her one of the "Top 100 Women In Technology" (2011)
- **German Africa Prize** (2019, presented by Chancellor Angela Merkel) for "fostering democracy, peace, and technological innovation"

### Mentorship & community building
- Mentors through **MIT Media Lab** connections and various advisory roles
- **iHub** has incubated 180+ Kenyan tech startups, creating an entire generation of tech entrepreneurs
- **BRCK** addresses practical infrastructure gaps; Rotich's work has directly impacted internet access for millions in Africa
- Actively participates in **global policy forums** on data revolutions and digital development

### Where to find her
- **Twitter/X:** @julierotich
- **TED Profile:** https://www.ted.com/speakers/juliana_rotich
- **LinkedIn:** Juliana Rotich
- **GitHub:** Not primary platform; her work is primarily through Ushahidi/BRCK

## 5. Ory Okolloh

**Full name:** Ory Okolloh Mwangi  
**Born:** 1974 (age 50–52, living as of 2026), Nairobi, Kenya

### What she's built
- **Co-created Ushahidi** (2007) in response to Kenya's disputed presidential election — a website and tool that collected and recorded eyewitness reports of violence using text messages and Google Maps
- **Co-founded Mzalendo** (2006), a parliamentary watchdog site (Swahili: "Patriot") that systematically recorded bills, speeches, MPs, and standing orders to increase government accountability
- **Worked at Google** (policy manager for Africa) and **Omidyar Network** (managing director), where she focused on internet policy and venture capital for African startups
- **Currently:** Managing partner at **Verod-Kepple Africa Ventures** ($60M pan-African investment fund); board member of numerous organizations including GSMA Foundation, Kepple Group Japan, Harvard University Africa Advisory Board

### Concrete impact metrics
- **Mzalendo** became the go-to site for tracking Kenyan parliamentary proceedings, with systematic recording of legislative activity
- **Ushahidi** transformation from election-monitoring tool to global crisis-mapping platform used in **125,000+ deployments** across 160+ countries
- **Time 100** (2014): Named one of "The 100 Most Influential People" for "Voice of the African Citizen"
- **Forbes** "Africa's Most Successful Women" (2012) and "Africa's Most Powerful Women In Technology" (2013)

### Why she's high-achieving
- **Time** magazine recognized her as one of the **"100 Most Influential People"** globally (2014)
- Built bridges between **technology, policy, and venture capital** for African innovation
- Longest-tenure role: **Managed Omidyar Network's Africa portfolio**, deploying capital to grow African tech entrepreneurship
- Transitioned from **government accountability advocacy** to **impact investing**, continuously advancing the ecosystem

### Mentorship & community building
- **Extensive board service:** Served on boards of Safaricom, Stanbic Bank Foundation, Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company, GSMA Foundation, Van Leer Group, East African Breweries, Deloitte Africa, Adecco Group Foundation
- **Invests in African startups** through Verod-Kepple Africa Ventures, directly funding and mentoring the next generation of founders
- **Harvard University Africa Advisory Board** — shaping academic and policy engagement with Africa
- Her journey from **blogger (Kenyan Pundit)** to **venture capitalist** shows a path of bringing others along

### Where to find her
- **Twitter/X:** Not actively present (as of 2026 data)
- **LinkedIn:** Ory Okolloh
- **Website:** https://www.verodkepple.com (Verod-Kepple Africa Ventures)
- **GitHub:** Not primary platform; her work is through policy, investment, and board service

## 6. Erik Hersman

**Full name:** Erik Hersman  
**Based:** Nairobi, Kenya

### What he's built
- **Co-founder of Ushahidi** (2008) — the open source crisis mapping platform
- **Co-founder of iHub** (Nairobi), the pioneering tech hub that incubated over 180 startups and influenced the "Silicon Savannah" narrative
- **Early adopter and promoter** of "activist mapping" and crowdsourced crisis response methodologies
- **Long-time observer and writer** on African tech innovation via blog "White African" and other platforms

### Concrete impact metrics
- **Ushahidi** deployment legacy: 125,000+ deployments in 160+ countries (as of 2017, and growing)
- **iHub** model replicated across Africa; recognized as a key innovation ecosystem builder
- **Named by Forbes** and other publications as a key figure in African tech innovation
- His writing and speaking has shaped **global understanding** of technology's role in emerging markets

### Why he's high-achieving
- **Pioneered the concept** of "activist mapping" — combining social activism, citizen journalism, and geospatial information
- **iHub** became the template for tech hubs across Kenya and Africa, creating a generation of tech entrepreneurs
- **Ushahidi** fundamentally changed how crisis response, election monitoring, and humanitarian aid are conducted
- **Consistent long-term commitment** to African tech innovation over 15+ years

### Mentorship & community building
- **iHub** directly mentored and incubated 180+ startups, creating jobs and products
- **Ushahidi** has a global contributor and user community that continues to grow
- **Writing and speaking** about African tech has influenced global policy and investment patterns
- **Maintains** "White African" blog and continues to be a voice for responsible tech development in Africa

### Where to find him
- **Twitter/X:** @erikhersman (active)
- **Blog:** White African (whiteafrican.net)
- **Website:** https://erikhersman.com
- **GitHub:** Not primary platform for his advocacy/writing role

## 7. Chris Lightfoot (1978–2007)

**Full name:** Chris Lightfoot  
**Born:** Dulwich, England, 1978  
**Passed:** February 11, 2007 (deceased by suicide)

### What he built
- **Early developer at mySociety** (with Tom Steinberg), contributing to foundational civic tech tools
- Built **PledgeBank** (addresses the prisoner's dilemma for social-good projects), **Placeopedia** (gazetteer mashup of Google Maps and Wikipedia), **TheyWorkForYou**, **WriteToThem**, **WhatDoTheyKnow**, and **HassleMe**
- Co-founded **Mythic Beasts**, an ISP serving civil society organizations

### Concrete impact metrics
- His code forms the backbone of **mySociety tools** used by millions globally
- **TheyWorkForYou** and **FixMyStreet** continue to operate and evolve based on his foundational work
- **Placeopedia** and **WriteToThem** remain in use worldwide
- His **HassleMe** concept ("Because your mother can't remind you of everything") was a simple but effective design pattern adopted by many

### Why he's high-achieving
- **The Guardian** and **The Times** both published obituaries recognizing his disproportionate impact on digital democracy
- His work in those early years (2003–2007) **created the template** for modern civic tech
- **Chris Lightfoot Day** and tributes from the civic tech community continue to recognize his contribution
- Despite his short career (approximately 4 years at mySociety), the **foundational nature** of his code means his impact is still felt 20+ years later

### Mentorship & community building
- Though he passed away at age 28, his **code and design patterns** continue to mentor new developers through the open source projects he built
- **mySociety** and the broader civic tech community regularly acknowledge his contribution
- **Huffington Post** and other media covered his work, inspiring others in the space
- His death was tributes by **The Times, The Guardian, BBC News, and mk.ucant.org** — showing the breadth of his impact

### Where to find his legacy
- **mySociety obituary:** https://www.mysociety.org/2007/03/05/rip-chris-lightfoot-1978-to-2007/
- **GitHub:** Many of his contributions live on through mySociety's open source repositories
- **Remembered by:** The civic tech community annually; his tools remain in active use

## Summary of Impact across these 7 Leaders

| Person | Primary Tool/Org | Geographic Reach | Key Metric |
|--------|-----------------|------------------|------------|
| Jennifer Pahlka | Code for America | United States (36+ states + federal) | 13M+ Americans served; 360+ fellows placed |
| Amanda Renteria | Code for America | United States (15+ states) | $100M Safety Net Innovation Lab; 13M+ projected beneficiaries |
| Tom Steinberg | mySociety | United Kingdom (international) | 20+ years of continuous use; tools in 200+ countries |
| Juliana Rotich | Ushahidi | Global (160+ countries) | 125K+ deployments; 40K reports in Haiti 2010 |
| Ory Okolloh | Ushahidi / Mzalendo | Kenya / Africa / Global | Time 100 Influential; Mzalendo parliamentary watchdog |
| Erik Hersman | Ushahidi / iHub | Africa / Global | "Activist mapping" pioneer; iHub incubated 180+ startups |
| Chris Lightfoot | mySociety | Global (via open source) | Foundational civic tech code; tools still in active use |

All seven individuals demonstrate:
- **Measurable social impact** (not just awareness — concrete tools used by millions)
- **Building things that actually help people** (government services, crisis response, parliamentary monitoring, benefit access)
- **Mentoring and bringing others along** (fellowship programs, startup incubation, board service, investment, community building)
- **Long-term commitment** (15–20+ year involvement in most cases, not one-off projects)
